A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from GRET to CATTE. Their methods, equations, experiments and appendices can be matched reliably. Visual inspection resolves extraction omissions, including v1's image-based Algorithm 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic rank-recovery experiments, predictions on three real-world datasets, ablations, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ablation results, noise-distribution tests, prior-hyperparameter sensitivity results and prediction case studies.

M1.justification: The proposed Fourier-feature encoder, latent ODE, decoder, Gaussian-Gamma priors, variational objective and prediction procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 also matches. GRET/CATTE and ARD/FARD are terminology changes.

E1.justification: The synthetic task and CA Traffic, Server Room and SSF datasets are retained. v2 adds synthetic evaluations with Laplacian and Poisson noise, extending the input-noise scenarios beyond Gaussian corruption (Appendix B.4, Table 5).

E2.justification: The six external baseline variants in Table 1 remain unchanged. v2 adds CATTE without FARD to that comparison; its GRET-without-ARD counterpart appeared only in the noise experiment in v1. Section 6.2 also changes the stated ablation objective from MSE to RMSE, without establishing a rerun.

E3.justification: New synthetic experiments sweep noise variances of 0.05, 0.10 and 0.15 and three prior-hyperparameter configurations (Tables 5 and 8). Existing split proportions, baseline rank grids and scalability settings are retained. The dataset attribution for Table 8 is inconsistent: its caption says synthetic data, whereas Section 6.2 says CA Traffic.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation with rank-adaptation ablations on all three main benchmarks, non-Gaussian noise tests, prior-hyperparameter sensitivity tests and twelve additional prediction cases (Figures 7–9). The earlier Gaussian-noise, ODE-dimension, rank-learning and scalability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages and standard deviations. v2 newly identifies the real-world repetitions as five-fold cross-validation, clarifying their interpretation without establishing an increase in runs. Additional result rows otherwise retain the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and matched noise, runtime and ODE-dimension results are unchanged. Substantial new results include the no-FARD RMSE values of 0.301, 0.091 and 0.402 in Table 1, noise and prior-sensitivity results in Tables 5 and 8, and prediction curves in Figures 7–9. These are added outcomes, not same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The factorization, probabilistic model, ELBO derivations and predictive-distribution mathematics are retained. v1 Section 4.2 moves to v2 Appendix A.7. The new Appendix C supplies qualitative comparisons rather than new mathematical definitions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the novelty positioning by explicitly asserting that existing classical rank-learning methods are inapplicable to functional tensors. The central claims about continuous-index modeling, automatic rank determination, sampling-free inference, predictive performance and noise robustness otherwise remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies the absence of explicit physical laws as a limitation. Appendix C adds explanations concerning memory scaling, simultaneous gradient updates and GPU parallelization relative to classical rank-learning approaches. Existing interpretations of recovered ranks and temporal patterns are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly claims supplementary code/data availability, which cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs. It removes CA Traffic's January 2018–December 2020 date window and the explicit statement that remaining real-world configurations follow the synthetic setup. Core implementation details, hardware, runtimes and Algorithm 1 are retained.

R1.justification: The citation attached to NONFAT changes from Wang et al.'s 'Nonparametric embeddings of sparse high-order interaction events' to Wang and Zhe's 'Nonparametric factor trajectory learning for dynamic tensor decomposition.' Appendix C also expands positioning against classical Bayesian rank determination. Consolidating duplicate Schmidt references does not remove that work.

P1.justification: The title, author list and method terminology change, with selective rewrites of motivation, inference and conclusions. Section 4.2 moves to Appendix A.7, and explanatory appendix material and a checklist are added. Most main-text prose and the principal section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially altering figure placement, sizing and text flow. v2 adds Figures 7–9 and Tables 5 and 8, expands Table 1, and relocates the former Table 3 as Table 7. Algorithm 1 is retypeset rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The added clean-data ablations test the central rank-adaptation component across all three benchmarks, while non-Gaussian noise tests probe robustness beyond the original Gaussian setting. The new physical-modeling limitation also improves qualification of the work. These provide useful gains over v1, although inconsistent dataset attribution for Table 8 and the unexplained MSE-to-RMSE ablation description limit the improvement in experimental transparency.
